subject: Pharmacology
vignette: A 38-year-old woman with episodic palpitations, diaphoresis, and headaches is found to have elevated plasma metanephrines and a 4-cm adrenal mass. She is started on an irreversible α-blocker before surgery to prevent a catecholamine (hypertensive) crisis.
question: Which of the following adverse effects is most expected during this preoperative therapy?

options.text: Increased serum cholesterol and increased appetite
Positive direct Coombs test with hemolysis
Orthostatic hypotension and reflex tachycardia
Dry mouth and generalized weakness
Cyanopia (blue-tinted vision)

explanation_correct: The drug is phenoxybenzamine, an irreversible nonselective α-blocker used preoperatively for pheochromocytoma to prevent catecholamine (hypertensive) crisis. Blocking α-mediated vasoconstriction causes orthostatic hypotension, and loss of the pressor response produces reflex tachycardia.

explanation_incorrect.A: Increased serum cholesterol and appetite are adverse effects of mirtazapine, an α2-selective blocker used for depression.
explanation_incorrect.B: Direct Coombs-positive hemolysis is a classic adverse effect of α-methyldopa, an α2-agonist used in pregnancy.
explanation_incorrect.D: Dry mouth (xerostomia) and weakness are adverse effects of tizanidine, an α2-agonist used for spasticity.
explanation_incorrect.E: Cyanopia (blue-tinted vision) occurs with sildenafil via PDE-6 inhibition in the retina.

educationalObjective: Phenoxybenzamine, an irreversible α-blocker for preoperative pheochromocytoma, causes orthostatic hypotension and reflex tachycardia.

subject: Pharmacology
vignette: A 52-year-old man on an MAO inhibitor attends a party and eats aged cheese and red wine. He develops a hypertensive crisis with a blood pressure of 230/125 mm Hg. Intravenous phentolamine is administered, and his blood pressure improves.
question: Which of the following best describes the mechanism and additional uses of the drug administered?

options.text: Reversible α-blocker; also used for severe cocaine-induced hypertension (2nd line) and norepinephrine extravasation
Irreversible α-blocker; also used preoperatively for pheochromocytoma and for chronic BPH symptoms
α2-selective blocker; also used for depression with sedation as a common adverse effect
α1-selective blocker; also used for PTSD nightmares and postural hypotension
β1-selective blocker; also used for supraventricular tachycardia and acute heart failure

explanation_correct: Phentolamine is a reversible nonselective α-blocker. It is given to patients on MAO inhibitors who ingest tyramine-containing foods (hypertensive crisis), for severe cocaine-induced hypertension as a second-line agent, and to treat norepinephrine extravasation.

explanation_incorrect.B: Irreversible α-blockade describes phenoxybenzamine, used preoperatively for pheochromocytoma; it is not used for BPH symptoms.
explanation_incorrect.C: α2-selective blockade with sedation describes mirtazapine, an antidepressant — not a treatment for hypertensive crisis.
explanation_incorrect.D: α1-selective blockers (-osins) treat BPH and PTSD (prazosin); they are not the reversible agent given in tyramine crises.
explanation_incorrect.E: β1-selective blockade describes metoprolol or esmolol for SVT; β-blockers would not reverse the α-mediated vasoconstriction in this crisis.

educationalObjective: Phentolamine is a reversible α-blocker for MAO-inhibitor/tyramine hypertensive crisis, severe cocaine-induced hypertension (2nd line), and norepinephrine extravasation.

subject: Pharmacology
vignette: A 66-year-old man takes his first dose of a newly prescribed oral α1-selective blocker at home. Thirty minutes later he stands up, feels lightheaded, and nearly syncopizes. He is brought to the emergency department and found to have marked orthostatic hypotension.
question: Which of the following best explains this patient's presentation?

options.text: Rebound hypertension from abrupt cessation of therapy
First-dose orthostatic hypotension due to α1-mediated vasodilation
Unopposed β2 activation after α1 blockade causing reflex bradycardia
Drug-induced lupus with autonomic involvement
Central respiratory depression and miosis from the drug

explanation_correct: α1-selective blockers (prazosin, terazosin, doxazosin, tamsulosin) are associated with first-dose orthostatic hypotension, dizziness, and headache. Blocking α1-mediated vasoconstriction impairs the normal compensatory vasoconstriction on standing, especially after the first dose.

explanation_incorrect.A: Rebound hypertension on abrupt cessation is associated with clonidine and guanfacine, not α1-blockers.
explanation_incorrect.C: α1-blockers do not cause reflex bradycardia through β2 activation; the problem here is impaired compensatory vasoconstriction with standing.
explanation_incorrect.D: Drug-induced lupus is associated with α-methyldopa, not α1-blockers.
explanation_incorrect.E: CNS depression, respiratory depression, and miosis are listed adverse effects of clonidine/guanfacine, not α1-blockers.

educationalObjective: First-dose orthostatic hypotension is the classic adverse effect of α1-selective blockers such as prazosin.

subject: Pharmacology
vignette: A 34-year-old combat veteran with post-traumatic stress disorder has recurrent distressing nightmares that disrupt sleep. His physician selects a specific α1-selective blocker that, unlike others in its class, is not used to treat hypertension.
question: Which of the following α1-selective blockers is most appropriate for this patient's nightmares?

options.text: Terazosin, used for BPH and hypertension
Tamsulosin, used for BPH but not hypertension
Doxazosin, used for BPH and hypertension
Prazosin, the -osin designated for PTSD
Mirtazapine, an α2-selective blocker used for depression

explanation_correct: Prazosin, terazosin, doxazosin, and tamsulosin are α1-selective (-osin) blockers used for urinary symptoms of BPH; hypertension is treated with the -osins except tamsulosin. Prazosin is specifically designated for PTSD, making it the best choice for trauma-related nightmares.

explanation_incorrect.A: Terazosin is a reversible α1-blocker used for BPH and hypertension, but it is not the -osin designated for PTSD nightmares.
explanation_incorrect.B: Tamsulosin is used for BPH and is the -osin excluded from hypertension use; it is not indicated for PTSD nightmares.
explanation_incorrect.C: Doxazosin is an α1-selective blocker used for hypertension and BPH, but not for PTSD.
explanation_incorrect.E: Mirtazapine is α2-selective (not α1) and used for depression, causing sedation, increased cholesterol, and increased appetite; it is not the α1-blocker for PTSD nightmares.

educationalObjective: α1-selective (-osin) blockers treat BPH; prazosin treats PTSD nightmares, and tamsulosin is the exception excluded from hypertension use.

subject: Pharmacology
vignette: A 41-year-old woman with major depressive disorder is started on an α2-selective antagonist. At follow-up she reports daytime sleepiness and increased hunger, and laboratory studies show a rise in serum cholesterol.
question: Which of the following best characterizes this drug's receptor selectivity and adverse-effect profile?

options.text: α1-selective; first-dose orthostatic hypotension and dizziness
α1-selective; reflex tachycardia and angina
Nonselective α-blockade; orthostatic hypotension with severe hypoglycemia
α2-selective; sedation, increased serum cholesterol, and increased appetite
β2-selective; tremor and bronchospasm

explanation_correct: The drug is mirtazapine, an α2-selective blocker used for depression. Its characteristic adverse effects are sedation, increased serum cholesterol, and increased appetite (weight gain) — matching this patient's presentation.

explanation_incorrect.A: First-dose orthostatic hypotension and dizziness belong to α1-selective blockers such as prazosin, terazosin, and doxazosin.
explanation_incorrect.B: Reflex tachycardia and orthostatic hypotension are seen with nonselective α-blockers such as phenoxybenzamine; mirtazapine is α2-selective.
explanation_incorrect.C: Nonselective α-blockade with orthostatic hypotension describes phenoxybenzamine/phentolamine; severe hypoglycemia masking is a β-blocker adverse effect.
explanation_incorrect.E: β2-selective agonists (not blockers) cause tremor; bronchospasm concern arises with β-blockade in asthma.

educationalObjective: Mirtazapine is an α2-selective blocker for depression causing sedation, increased cholesterol, and increased appetite.
